title: Best Social Media Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a social media designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: Social media design covers the posts, stories, carousels and banners that make your feed look like one brand. The common problems are designs made in the wrong sizes, templates you cannot edit, and images the designer had no right to use. This guide helps you order designs you can keep using.

faq.a: It depends on the platforms. Square and 4:5 portrait posts suit feeds, 9:16 suits stories and reels, and profile banners have their own sizes. List every platform and format in your brief so nothing needs to be resized later.
Ask for them. Templates in a tool you can use, such as Canva, or layered source files, let you change text and photos yourself for future posts.

faq.q: Does the designer write the captions?
faq.a: Usually not. Social media design packages cover the images. Captions, hashtags and posting are normally part of social media management, which is a separate service.

faq.q: Can the designer use stock photos?
faq.a: Yes, if they are properly licensed for commercial use. Ask where the images come from, and prefer your own product photos where possible.

faq.q: How many designs should I order?
faq.a: Start with a small set that covers your main post types, such as a quote post, a product post and an announcement. Once you are happy with the style, reuse the templates.
